config_apply_external_tip: Install what the external tool wrote to %merged
config_discard_new_tip: Delete the .pacnew and keep your current file unchanged
config_external_tip: Open in the external merge tool
config_identical_explain: The .pacnew is byte-for-byte identical to your current file. It's safe to remove.
config_oversize: This file is too large for the in-panel merge. Use the external merge tool, take the new version as-is, or discard it.
config_pacsave_explain: This file's package was removed. pacman kept your edited config as a .pacsave. Restore it to put it back in place, or remove it.

config_summary.one: 1 conflict to resolve — everything else is merged automatically
config_summary.other: {count} conflicts to resolve — everything else is merged automatically

config_summary_clean: No conflicts — the new default's changes merge in cleanly. Preview, then apply.
config_summary_nobase: No common ancestor found — every difference is shown as a choice.
config_take_new_full_tip: Replace your file with the package's new default
config_unreadable_explain: This file isn't readable without root, so the in-panel merge can't open it. Use the external tool (it escalates via sudo) or remove the .pacnew.

err_terminal_closed: The terminal window closed before the update finished, check the log or retry in a terminal

launcher.check_subtitle: Check pacman, AUR and Flatpak for updates
launcher.news_subtitle: Open the Arch Linux news page
launcher.update_subtitle: Install the pending updates (terminal or background, per the update mode setting)

log_waiting: Waiting for the polkit password prompt and the first output…

notify_config_new.one: An update left 1 new .pacnew file to review
notify_config_new.other: An update left {count} new .pacnew files to review

notify_polkit_ok: Polkit rule installed: one password per update run from now on
polkit_hint: Polkit asks for a password several times per update
reboot_recommended: Reboot recommended, the running kernel is no longer installed
rollback_missing: The old version is no longer in the pacman/AUR cache

activity_history_length.description: How many of the most recent checks to keep for the activity graph.
activity_history_length.label: Activity history length

assume_yes.description: Pass --noconfirm / -y so package managers do not ask for confirmation. Off means you confirm each one in the terminal window.
assume_yes.label: Answer yes automatically

aur_check_cmd.description: Only used when the AUR helper above is 'Custom command'. Must print one 'name oldver -> newver' line per package, like 'yay -Qua' does.
aur_check_cmd.label: Custom AUR check command

aur_helper.description: Which AUR helper checks and upgrades AUR packages. 'Auto-detect' tries yay, then paru. 'Custom command' lets you supply your own check command below.
aur_helper.label: AUR helper

auto_check_hours.description: Check for updates automatically every N hours. 0 (default) never checks on its own.
auto_check_hours.label: Auto-check interval (hours)

check_arch_news.description: Fetch the Arch Linux news feed and flag unread posts in the panel.
check_arch_news.label: Check Arch Linux news

check_reboot_needed.description: Detect whether the currently running kernel's files are still on disk. When they are gone, a newer kernel was installed and a reboot is what switches you to it.
check_reboot_needed.label: Check if a reboot is needed

config_auto_remove_identical.description: After an update run, delete .pacnew files that are byte-for-byte identical to the live file, in a single polkit prompt. Off keeps them in the list with a one-click Remove.
config_auto_remove_identical.label: Auto-remove identical .pacnew

config_backup.description: Save a copy of the current config before writing the merged result.
config_backup.label: Back up the file before applying

config_backup_dir.description: Empty: a 'config-backups' folder in the plugin's data directory. An absolute path: back up there. 'alongside': keep a <file>.arch-updater.bak next to each file (owned by root).
config_backup_dir.label: Backup location

config_backup_keep.description: Prune older backups beyond this many per file. 0 keeps all. Ignored for the 'alongside' location.
config_backup_keep.label: Backups to keep per file

config_badge.description: Show the count of pending .pacnew/.pacsave files on the bar widget when no updates are pending.
config_badge.label: Config-review badge

config_default_resolution.description: Which side each conflicting hunk starts on in the merge view. 'Keep my version' never changes a line you edited; 'Take the new version' prefers the package's new default.
config_default_resolution.label: Default choice for conflicts

config_diff_tool.description: Command for 'View diff', with tokens %a (current file) and %b (.pacnew). Empty uses 'diff' in the terminal pager.
config_diff_tool.label: External diff viewer

config_include_pacsave.description: Include .pacsave files (a removed package's kept config) in the review list, with restore and remove actions.
config_include_pacsave.label: Also list .pacsave files

config_merge_tool.description: Command to open instead of the built-in merge. Tokens: %mine %base %theirs %merged. Example: meld %mine %merged %theirs. Empty uses the in-panel merge.
config_merge_tool.label: External merge tool

config_notify.description: Send a notification when an update run leaves new .pacnew files behind.
config_notify.label: Notify about new .pacnew files

config_review.description: After each check and each update, scan for pacman's .pacnew/.pacsave files and offer an in-panel 3-way merge. Off also stops the scan and hides the bar badge.
config_review.label: Review .pacnew config files

config_search_paths.description: Absolute directories to scan for .pacnew/.pacsave/.pacorig files. Default: /etc.
config_search_paths.label: Config search paths

flatpak_enabled.description: Also check (and, on Update, run) 'flatpak update'. Ignored automatically when flatpak is not installed.
flatpak_enabled.label: Include Flatpak

glyph.description: The glyph shown for the widget on the bar.
glyph.label: Bar glyph

hide_on_empty.description: Hide the widget entirely when there are no pending updates and no reboot recommendation. Off (default) always shows the glyph.
hide_on_empty.label: Hide when there is nothing to show

hide_polkit_hint.description: Hide the panel line offering to install the polkit keep-authorization rule (one password per update run).
hide_polkit_hint.label: Hide the polkit rule suggestion

ignore_packages.description: Package names to leave out of the count and pass as --ignore to the update itself, in addition to pacman.conf's own IgnorePkg.
ignore_packages.label: Ignore packages

log_lines.description: How many of the latest update-log lines the panel shows while an update is running.
log_lines.label: Log lines in the panel

notify_on_updates.description: Send a desktop notification when a check finds packages to upgrade.
notify_on_updates.label: Notify when updates are found

rollback_auto_ignore.description: After a successful rollback, add the rolled-back packages to the plugin's ignore list so the next check does not immediately offer them again.
rollback_auto_ignore.label: Ignore packages after a rollback

show_activity_graph.description: Track pending-update counts across recent checks and when you last updated, shown as a small graph above the update history strip. Off (default) also stops recording the history.
show_activity_graph.label: Show activity graph

show_changelog_after_update.description: Open the panel's changelog automatically once an update run finishes successfully.
show_changelog_after_update.label: Show changelog after updating

show_count.description: Show the number of pending updates next to the bar glyph.
show_count.label: Show the update count

show_download_size.description: Estimate the total download size for the pending pacman packages with 'pacman -Si'. AUR and Flatpak sizes are not included.
show_download_size.label: Show download size

terminal.description: Terminal command for terminal-mode updates and the 'Retry in terminal' fallback, e.g. kitty or ghostty. Empty (default) uses Noctalia's terminal detection ($TERMINAL, then the common emulators).
terminal.label: Terminal

update_cmd.description: Full override for the update command, in both terminal and background mode. Empty (default) builds it from the AUR helper, ignore list and Flatpak settings above.
update_cmd.label: Custom update command

update_mode.description: How the Update button runs the upgrade. 'In a terminal window' (default) behaves like the original plugin: prompts and the PKGBUILD review work as usual. 'In the background' is fully non-interactive (--noconfirm, review skipped) with a live log in the panel.
update_mode.label: Update mode

tip_changelog: See what's new in each release
tip_history_segment: Click to see this run's packages
tip_ignore: Ignore this package: hide it from the count and skip it on update
tip_polkit_install: Install the polkit rule so updates can run in the background with one password prompt
tip_rollback: Roll back to {version}, together with its dependencies from this run. pacman refuses the whole transaction if it would break other packages.
tip_rollback_run: Downgrade every package of this run in one transaction
tip_run_terminal: Open a terminal window where prompts work normally
tip_update: Update in the background: polkit asks for your password, everything else is automatic
tip_update_terminal: Update in a terminal window: prompts and the PKGBUILD review work as usual
title: Arch Updater
